Structure Formation and Distillation in VecSet Latent Space

Branch: exp/distill-methods-v2 • Date: 2026-04-08 • Hunyuan3D-2.1 (50-step flow matching) • Toys4k dataset
Overview Methodology ODE Analysis Latent Dynamics Method Comparison Synthesis Related Work Limitations & Next Steps

1. Overview

This report combines two experiments to answer: why does distillation work for 3D generation, and what are its limits? First, we decode the teacher's intermediate ODE states to observe how 3D structure forms in the VecSet latent space. Then, we evaluate five distillation methods and connect their performance to the structure formation dynamics.

CFG Robustness Check

The ODE trajectory was initially run with CFG=7.5 (training config) instead of 5.0 (teacher inference). Re-running with CFG=5.0 shows: 8/10 samples have identical crystallization step; 2 samples shift by 1 step later. Final CD at step 50 differs by <12%. The three-phase structure is robust to this variation.

Chamfer Distance vs ODE Progress

Log-scale CD to ground truth at each step. The blue band marks the crystallization zone (t=0.5–0.7) where structure rapidly emerges.

Finding 1: Crystallization at t = 0.5–0.6

For t < 0.4, the latent contains no decodable structure (marching cubes fails entirely). At t = 0.5–0.6, global structure abruptly appears. Simple shapes (ball, apple) crystallize earlier (t = 0.4) than complex ones (helicopter, robot: t = 0.6).

Finding 2: CD converges by t = 0.7

After t = 0.7 (step 35), Chamfer distance barely changes. The final 30% of ODE steps contribute almost nothing to geometric quality. This means the last 15 steps out of 50 are refinement of already-formed structure.

Finding 3: Complexity determines crystallization timing

Simple convex shapes (ball, apple) emerge at t = 0.4. Medium complexity (cup, shoe, chair) at t = 0.5. Complex articulated shapes (robot, helicopter) require t = 0.6. Distillation must preserve fidelity during each shape's critical crystallization window.

4. Latent Space Dynamics: Three Phases of Structure Formation

Beyond mesh decoding, we analyze the latent vectors directly to understand what the teacher is computing at each ODE step. Three distinct phases emerge.

Phase I (t=0.0–0.4): Homogeneous Contraction — Noise Purification

The latent L2 norm decreases by 21% (463 → 367). Cross-sample cosine similarity is 0.999+ — ball, chair, and helicopter are virtually identical in latent space. PCA shows all samples clustered together. The VAE volume decoder outputs uniformly −1.0 everywhere: "there is no object." The model is removing high-frequency noise while all samples converge to a shared pre-structural state. Sample-specific information has not yet been injected into the latent.

Phase II (t=0.4–0.6): Crystallization — Structural Phase Transition

Cross-sample similarity drops sharply (0.99 → 0.94). PCA shows samples separating into distinct clusters. Volume logits develop zero-crossings (isosurfaces appear). The ODE trajectory shows maximum deviation from a straight line in this interval — the flow is "bending" as conditioning information forces differentiation. This is the critical window where the model decides what shape to create.

Phase III (t=0.6–1.0): Refinement & Scaling

Chamfer distance converges. Volume logit statistics stabilize. Token norms increase monotonically (365 → 510) but spatial structure doesn't change. PCA positions are stable. The model is scaling up the amplitude of already-formed structure without modifying topology.

Runtime Breakdown

Volume decoding (~9s) dominates wall-clock time. Step reduction from 50→1 saves only ~4.5s (28%).

Complementary Failures: CD vs DMD1

CD (4-step) and DMD1 (1-step) have complementary strengths — neither dominates on all categories. This suggests fundamentally different failure modes, not simply "more steps = better."

6. Synthesis: Connecting ODE Dynamics to Distillation

Why CD (4-step) wins

With 4 steps, the ODE visits t = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Two points fall in the crystallization zone (t = 0.5 and 0.75), and consistency distillation enforces self-consistency along the full trajectory. This covers the critical structure formation phase while maintaining trajectory coherence.

Why 1-step is harder than it looks

The crystallization at t = 0.5–0.6 is an abrupt phase transition, not a gradual process. A 1-step model must compress this discontinuity into a single forward pass. DMD1 succeeds partially by using pre-computed teacher pairs as regression targets (sidestepping the trajectory entirely). DMD2 fails because adversarial loss alone cannot capture this transition.

Volume decode is the real bottleneck

Even with 1-step diffusion (0.1s), total inference is 11s because VAE decode takes ~9s. Step reduction has hit diminishing returns. The next frontier is decoder acceleration (FlashVDM approach: hierarchical decode + adaptive KV selection achieves 45× decode speedup).

PD Stages vs Crystallization

PD StageStepsCoverageCrystallization
Stage 150 → 25t sampled every 0.04Full coverage, but most steps in post-convergence zone
Stage 225 → 12t sampled every 0.082-3 points in crystallization zone
Stage 312 → 6t sampled every 0.171-2 points in crystallization zone, error accumulates

PD's cascaded error accumulation across 3 stages explains why it underperforms CD despite using more steps (6 vs 4). A possible improvement: skip directly from 50 to 12 steps, then 12 to 6 (2-stage instead of 3).

Connection to LATTICE (Lai et al., CVPR 2026)

LATTICE argues that VecSet tokens lack spatial structure, and introducing positional encoding (VoxSet) enables Scaling Law. Our Phase I data supports this directly: at t < 0.4, cross-sample cosine similarity is 0.999+ and PCA variance is near-random (PC10 = 18.7% vs 15.6% for uniform). The VecSet latent space is structureless during noise purification. Structure only emerges through conditioning at Phase II — and once it does, it is implicit and fragile (FlashVDM found only ~10 tokens per query are attended to).

Connection to FlashVDM (ICCV 2025 Highlight)

FlashVDM discovered that VecSet VAE attention maps have strong spatial locality. Our trajectory straightness (S > 0.91) is consistent with this, though recent work (“Straightness Is Not Your Need,” ICLR 2025) argues straightness is descriptive rather than causal for distillation success. What matters more: the consistency constraint (our CD method’s key advantage) and Phase II coverage. FlashVDM’s guidance distillation warmup is essential precisely because it prepares the student for the crystallization transition.

Novel Contribution

No prior work has decoded intermediate ODE states of a 3D LDM to study structure formation dynamics. Our three-phase characterization, VAE attention analysis, and controlled distillation comparison provide the first experimental bridge between latent space geometry theory (Park, DC-AE) and practical distillation design (FlashVDM, Consistency Models) in the 3D generation domain.

8. Limitations & Next Steps

Limitations

  • Single base model: All results are for Hunyuan3D-2.1 (VecSet). Sparse Voxel models (Trellis, Trellis2) may show different dynamics due to built-in spatial structure.
  • Small scale: N=10 trajectory samples, N=420 training data, LoRA rank 64. Production distillation operates at orders of magnitude larger scale.
  • Simple dataset: Toys4k objects are geometrically simple compared to Objaverse diversity.
  • No ICP alignment in trajectory CD: Absolute CD values from intermediate decode are not comparable to ICP-aligned evaluations. Relative trends across steps remain valid.
  • Mean pooling: Latent analysis (PCA, t-SNE) uses mean-pooled tokens, losing token-level sparsity dynamics.

Next Steps

  • Sparse Voxel comparison: Run the same trajectory analysis on Trellis2 to test whether the three-phase structure is VecSet-specific or universal to 3D LDMs.
  • Teacher step-quality curve: Run teacher at 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 25 steps (no distillation) to isolate distillation’s contribution from simple step reduction.
  • Token-level dynamics: Analyze per-token norm distributions and activation patterns to complement mean-pooled analysis.
  • Riemannian metric analysis: Apply Park et al.’s pullback metric to 3D VecSet latent space to quantify geometry changes across phases.
  • 2-stage PD: Test [50→12], [12→6] to reduce error accumulation.
